title: A year and a half ago, I was barely taking care of myself.
hook: A year and a half ago, I was barely taking care of myself.
caption:
A year and a half ago, I was barely taking care of myself.

I was inconsistent, stressed, sleeping badly, barely eating, relying on caffeine, and doing anything I could just to get through the day. My physique changed, but honestly that was the smallest part of what was falling apart.

January 2025 became the point where I had to choose whether I was going to keep sinking or start rebuilding.

So I started small. I fixed my sleep, ate properly again, trained consistently, cut back on the things I was abusing, and started putting my own health and peace first.

The physical progress came later.

title: 🏋️ Strength training after 40 needs a whole new playbook.
hook: 🏋️ Strength training after 40 needs a whole new playbook.
caption:
🏋️ Strength training after 40 needs a whole new playbook.

The high volume routines younger lifters thrive on? They'll burn you out or hurt you past forty. Hormones and recovery rates drop with age, so the better move is training that builds muscle protein while keeping inflammation low.

🛡️ Your joints deserve more respect too.

Tendons lose elasticity over time, so skip the explosive, joint-shocking lifts. A few habits change the game:

title: Leg day is the best day. 😳👀
hook: Leg day is the best day. 😳👀
caption:
Leg day is the best day. 😳👀

Yeah, I said it.

I know that’s probably a hot take, but there’s nothing more rewarding than watching your legs grow. They’re one of the hardest muscle groups to build, and every session feels earned.

I’m still putting a lot of focus on my posterior chain and bringing up my hamstrings and glutes. I’m really proud of how my quads are developing.

Even halfway through this bulk, they’re staying lean and showing more detail than I expected.

Leg day isn’t punishment.

It’s a privilege.

Keep evolving. 🦖
